Ahold Delhaize stock weighs cyber hit on 2026 outlook
sum: Ahold Delhaize said on Wednesday, November 4, that an October cybersecurity incident will weigh on fourth-quarter performance and has prompted a weaker 2026 outlook. The company expects the disruption to reduce fourth-quarter net sales by EUR 200 million to EUR 250 million and underlying and IFRS operating income by EUR 75 million to EUR 100 million, according to its official results release.

The group now expects diluted underlying earnings per share to grow at a low-single-digit rate at constant exchange rates, compared with its previous mid- to high-single-digit forecast. Free cash flow guidance was reduced to around EUR 2.1 billion from at least EUR 2.3 billion. The underlying operating margin is expected to approach 4.0%, versus previous guidance of around 4.0%.

Management said the incident mainly affected online operations in the Benelux and the United States, as well as Benelux supply-chain activities. Most disruption was contained within two weeks, while restoration work continues. The company also cited new supplier payment regulations in Serbia in its free-cash-flow outlook.

Third-quarter net sales reached EUR 23.1 billion, up 1.9% at constant exchange rates. Online sales increased 8.2%, including 14.2% growth in the United States. Underlying operating margin was 4.1%, while IFRS operating income reached EUR 976 million. The IFRS result was EUR 30 million above the underlying result, mainly because of a pension settlement in the United States.

Ahold Delhaize also announced that its EUR 1 billion annual share buyback program will continue in 2027 and said it expects to increase the 2026 dividend per share at a mid-single-digit rate based on the revised outlook. For investors, the key issue is whether digital services and supply-chain operations normalize before the important holiday trading period.
Ahold Delhaize stock traded at EUR 34.14 on Lang & Schwarz at 18:03 CET on Friday, November 6. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Ahold Delhaize stock.

Is Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize (ENXTAM:AD) Cheap After Its Cyberattack?
sum: Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize has delivered a 3 year share price gain that will catch most investors' attention, yet recent setbacks and investments leave a practical question: Is the current price really supported by the cash this grocery group is expected to generate over time, or is the market leaning too heavily on the recent share performance and headlines?
- The stock is up 43.8% over 3 years. This puts real weight on whether that advance is aligned with the cash flows the business can produce.

- The cyberattack that Ahold Delhaize expects to reduce net sales by €200 million to €250 million and keep its operating margin closer to 4% may reshape how investors think about the resilience and trajectory of future cash flows.

items.t: Ahold Delhaize Earnings Call: Growth Meets Cyber Risk
[Ahold Delhaize Q3 2026 Earnings Call] Cyberattack to Cut €200-250M from Q4 Sales, Full-Year Margin Outlook Trimmed to ~4%
sum: Ahold Delhaize reported third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, but the headline was overshadowed by a cybersecurity incident that struck in October, forcing the retailer to take systems offline and prompting a downgrade to its full-year outlook. The company now expects an underlying operating margin approaching 4%, down from previous guidance, and free cash flow of around €2.1 billion, a €200 million reduction.

CEO Frans Muller opened the call by addressing the cyber incident directly. "We apologize to our customers for the disruption and inconvenience and are grateful for their trust, loyalty, and understanding," he said. "Cyber threats are an increasingly harsh reality of doing business today."

CFO Jolanda Poots-Bijl quantified the impact: Q4 net sales will be reduced by €200-250 million, and underlying operating income by €75-100 million. Approximately 80% of the sales hit is in Europe, particularly the Netherlands, while the profit impact is more balanced due to mitigation efforts. The incident affected online capabilities in the Benelux and U.S., as well as parts of the Benelux supply chain, though bol was not impacted.

"The underlying operating income impact is based on many elements next to the regular sales flow-through. For example, it's shrink, extra hours worked to get supply running, promotional actions to welcome our customers back, and the negative impact on, for example, lost vendor allowances and retail media," Poots-Bijl explained.

Despite the cyber overhang, the underlying quarter showed resilience. Net sales rose 1.9% to €23.1 billion, helped by a 15 basis point positive impact from weather and calendar shifts. Underlying operating margin dipped 10 basis points to 4.1%, as a favorable discounting effect on insurance provisions at group level was offset by a modest decline in the U.S. Diluted underlying EPS increased 1% to €0.69, supported by higher operating profit and share buybacks, partially offset by higher financial expenses.
U.S. Performance: Positive Volumes, Market Share Gains Despite Headwinds
In the U.S., net sales reached €13.3 billion, with comparable sales growth of 0.5% excluding gasoline.

Cyberattack on supermarket fridges spreads across Europe, spoils food stocks
sum: The latest cyberattack, which echoed a similar incident in France last month, targeted supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg and Ireland.

A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize, and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.
"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."
A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems."

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

Ahold Delhaize stock drops as November 4 results approach
sum: Ahold Delhaize stock traded lower on Monday as investors looked ahead to the group's third-quarter results on November 4. The latest company calendar confirms the release date, while the share has moved materially below the level cited in the previous report.

Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 31.98 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 2:39:20 p.m. CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 2.53 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The comparison uses the Friday Xetra close of 32.81 euros identified for the AHOG listing by De Belegger.

Since the previous October 30 report, which cited a Lang & Schwarz price of 33.13 euros, the share has declined 3.47 percent. This is a market comparison rather than a statement about the cause of the move.

Ahold Delhaize's investor-relations calendar lists third-quarter 2026 results for November 4, 2026. The company published its second-quarter results on August 5, making the upcoming release the next scheduled checkpoint for revenue, profitability and the outlook.

The results will be particularly relevant for investors tracking the group's operating margin and sales momentum. A fresh quarter should show whether the trends discussed ahead of the release are reflected in reported performance.

On October 30, Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak businesses to Ahold Delhaize. The transaction covers stores, offices and distribution centres in both countries, while Tesco's Hungarian operations are excluded.

Completion requires antitrust and other regulatory approvals and is expected in the second half of 2027. Tesco expects to return most net proceeds through an additional share buyback after completion and expects the transaction to be broadly neutral to earnings per share and its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio after the buyback.

Ahold Delhaize stock faces margin test before November 4 results
sum: Ahold Delhaize is due to publish its third-quarter results on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The update will give investors a fresh read on trading in the United States and Europe after concerns about softer volumes and falling food prices in the Netherlands.
Ahold Delhaize stock traded at 32.95 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:06 CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Ahold Delhaize stock.

RBC Capital Markets expects profit margins to tighten in the third quarter, according to Finimize. The bank cited softer US grocery volumes, Dutch food-price deflation and pressure on fresh-produce sales.

RBC models a combined 1.6 percentage-point hit to third-quarter performance from reduced US food-aid benefits, egg-price deflation and changes affecting pharmacy profits under the Inflation Reduction Act. The bank also cut its price target to 37 euros from 38 euros and reduced longer-term forecasts for underlying pretax profit, dividend per share and earnings per share by 1% to 2%.

The results should show how Ahold Delhaize balances traffic, promotions and profitability when lower prices limit the contribution from inflation. The key operating questions are whether US demand stabilized and whether the Dutch business protected volumes without giving up too much margin.
